solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Isn't beginning to discount danger, trembling and deeply worried

indicators.note: trembling letters are shaken out of place and settle in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: first letter of discount
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who has stopped playing down a threat is now shaking with anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: All eleven letters of ISNT, D and DANGER are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst-ridden means consumed by anxiety and dread, a close synonym of deeply worried.

clue.text: Heat varies in lofted space, less squelchy part of bog

indicators.note: in a down clue, lofted means lifted upward, so the word is read from the bottom up
in places one set of letters inside the other

parts.note: a gap is a space

indicators.note: something that varies takes on a different form, so the letters change order

parts.note: the letters of heat rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about warmth in an attic, followed by a note on boggy ground.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the space word reads upwards, and the rearranged heat sits within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A peat hag is a firmer mound or bank of peat standing among the wetter parts of a bog.

clue.text: In pash being thwarted by female, showing cunning about that aid to better sex (10, two words)

indicators.note: plans that are thwarted are upset and thrown into disorder
about means surrounding, so one word wraps round the rest

parts.note: sly means cunning
the letters of in pash rearranged
F is the standard abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A crush is frustrated by a woman, prompting someone to sneakily reach for an aphrodisiac.
explanation.walkthrough: Pash is slang for a crush or infatuation; here it is just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish fly is a preparation from blister beetles long reputed to be an aphrodisiac, a supposed sexual stimulant.

clue.text: Never stood for spicy meat en brochette

indicators.note: one thing standing for another means it takes the other's place

parts.note: split as N plus ever, and ay is an old word for ever
stood for office is sat, as for a parliamentary seat

explanation.surface: Someone declares they never tolerated skewered spiced meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Read Never as N + EVER, with EVER as AY; then SAT takes the place of the N. The blog's own parse of this clue is unsure.
explanation.definitionFit: Satay is a South-East Asian dish of spiced meat grilled on skewers, which is what en brochette means.

clue.text: Bit of immature creature, part replacing one in farm animal

indicators.note: replacing means one item is taken out and another put in its place

parts.note: a pig is a farm animal
the Roman numeral for one, removed
a part in a play is a role

explanation.surface: A description of swapping something within a farm animal, framed as a piece of a young creature.
explanation.walkthrough: ROLE takes the place of the I in PIG.
explanation.definitionFit: A proleg is one of the fleshy stubby legs on the abdomen of a caterpillar or other larva.

clue.text: What's mass of clay in New York, producing a sort of 'bong'?

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: standard abbreviation
argil is potter's clay

explanation.surface: A quizzical question about clay in New York and a drug pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A nargily, a variant spelling of narghile, is a Middle Eastern water pipe, like the bong used for smoking.

clue.text: Water running into shore's rotten — could be 'dead' hippo

indicators.note: running into means going inside, so one word enters the other
something rotten has fallen apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
ea is a dialect word for a river or running water

explanation.surface: Water floods a decaying coastline, where maybe a dead hippo washes up.
explanation.walkthrough: Hippo in the definition is short for hippocampus, a mythical sea monster, and 'dead' nods to the Dead Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippocampus, Greek for sea-horse, is both the seahorse genus and a mythical sea creature; with 'dead' the hint suggests a Dead Sea horse.

clue.text: Chorale may be translated from this odist, Latin

indicators.note: translation turns words into a different form, here a different letter order

parts.note: taken as written: the whole fodder
L is the abbreviation for Latin; it is the extra letter in the fodder

explanation.surface: A sung chorale could be rendered from a Latin poet's ode.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: the answer plus L together rearrange to CHORALE. The Roman poet Horace wrote in Latin and set odes to music, so translating him could yield a chorale.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace is the Roman lyric poet famous for his Odes, so he is the odist in question.

clue.text: I'll escape from a fire that's activated alarm

indicators.note: something activated is set in motion, so the letters move around
escaping from somewhere means leaving it, so that letter goes

parts.note: the speaker, I, is the letter removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone vows to run out of a burning building whose alarm has gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the I out of A FIRE and rearrange what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm as a noun means sudden fright or dread, a synonym of fear.

clue.text: Recommended by dieticians — unlike much of what it serves?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, split into two: low-calorie, what a diet adviser approves

definitions.text: unlike much of what it serves
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a neighbourhood pub, whose beer is hardly slimming

explanation.walkthrough: Read the first way the answer is LO-CAL, low in calories; the second is the British pub around the corner, which serves plenty that is not low-calorie.
explanation.definitionFit: Lo-cal is a contraction of low-calorie, while your local is the nearby pub you regularly drink in.

clue.text: Strong wind battered range — bitter? (8, two words)

indicators.note: battered means knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of range rearranged
bitter is a type of British beer, an ale

explanation.surface: A fierce wind lashed the mountain range, and it was bitterly cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitter' looks like a description of the wind, but it is the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A near gale is force 7 on the Beaufort scale, a strong wind just short of a full gale.

clue.text: Falconer's bird? Deal in the latest, cracking experience mostly

indicators.note: cracking something open lets other letters get inside it
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to taste is to experience
to deal in goods is to sell them
gen is slang for up-to-date information

explanation.surface: A falconry question, then a picture of someone trading in the newest goods and gaining most of the experience.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information. Tassell-gent, or tassel-gentle, is an old falconry name.
explanation.definitionFit: A tassell-gent is an old term for a tercel, the male hawk used in falconry.

clue.text: It lurks in the everglades from Georgia to heart of Florida

parts.note: GA is the US state abbreviation for Georgia
taken as written

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

parts.note: the middle letter of the seven

explanation.surface: A creature skulks in the swamps stretching from Georgia down into Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: the Everglades lie in southern Florida, near Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: A gator, short for alligator, is the large reptile typically lying in wait in the Florida swamps.

clue.text: Fellow managed prison (all names withheld) — it maintains a lively rhythm

indicators.note: names withheld means each N, the abbreviation for name, is removed

parts.note: a fellow is a man
to manage a business is to run it
the can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A man ran a jail where nobody's identity was disclosed.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN RAN CAN each lose their N.
explanation.definitionFit: A maraca is a gourd rattle shaken in Latin American music to keep up a brisk beat.

clue.text: Site that is missing a prisoner? Not one for that kind

definitions.text: Site that is missing a prisoner? Not one for that kind

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so those letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is; removed
taken as written
an old lag is a long-serving prisoner

explanation.surface: Is this a place lacking an inmate? No, never one with that sort.
explanation.walkthrough: SITE minus IE leaves ST. Read as a whole, the clue describes a camp that was anything but missing prisoners.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp in the Second World War, a site always full of captives.

clue.text: Narcotic, one featuring in dailies

indicators.note: featuring in means appearing inside, so one goes within the other

parts.note: dailies and chars are both British terms for cleaning ladies
a means one

explanation.surface: A drug appears in the daily newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dailies' wants to be newspapers; it is daily cleaners, called chars in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Charas is hashish, the resin of the cannabis plant, used as a drug.

clue.text: Face mostly disfigured with boils? They can change the way one looks

definitions.text: They can change the way one looks

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter goes
disfigured means spoilt in shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: face without its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A face scarred with spots might well alter someone's appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on looks: appearance in the surface, the act of looking in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bifocals are spectacles with two-part lenses, altering how the wearer sees, near or far.

clue.text: Awful mess — double-headed besom's wielded with it

indicators.note: a broom that is wielded is swung about, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: besom with its first letter doubled
taken as written

explanation.surface: A terrible mess is left, swept with a two-headed broom.
explanation.walkthrough: A besom is a broom of twigs; 'double-headed' doubles its leading B.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombsite, literally ground wrecked by bombing, is used figuratively for any dreadfully untidy place.

clue.text: Slating material, furious in being written out

indicators.note: words written out of a text are struck from it

parts.note: raging means furious
taken as written; removed

explanation.surface: A critic's damning review, furious as it is written up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slating' suggests harsh criticism; here it is roofing. Rag, or ragg, is a hard coarse stone that splits into roofing slates.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragg is a variant of rag, a hard rough stone that can be split for roofing slates.

clue.text: Choirboy to quiver missing mass

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the letter goes

parts.note: to tremble is to quiver
M is the symbol for mass; removed

explanation.surface: A young chorister shakes nervously, having missed Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: Mass looks like the church service, which fits a choirboy; it is the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A treble is a boy singing the highest voice part in a choir.

clue.text: Isotope: it's discovered in notable achievement, independent of pH

indicators.note: independent of means without, so those letters are removed
something discovered in a place has been found inside it

parts.note: a triumph is a great success
taken as written
taken as written; removed

explanation.surface: A chemist's boast: an isotope found in a great breakthrough that has nothing to do with acidity.
explanation.definitionFit: Tritium is the radioactive isotope of hydrogen with two neutrons in its nucleus.

clue.text: Beneficiary set up a limit for trust maybe

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to gel is to set, as a jelly does
taken as written

indicators.note: a limit of a word is one of its end letters

parts.note: an end letter of trust, written out as tee
the letter-name tee supplies two more letters

explanation.surface: A beneficiary arranged a cap on a trust fund.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter T, a limit of trust, is spelled out as the word TEE. 'Trust' looks like the legal kind for a beneficiary; it only supplies its end letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A legatee is a person who inherits a legacy under a will, a type of beneficiary.

clue.text: Former disgrace, portent (not the first) — goodness me!

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a sign is a portent; it loses its S
oh my, an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: An old scandal, an ill omen, and someone gasping in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: SIGN minus S gives IGN; 'O my!' is a version of 'Oh my!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignomy is an obsolete form of ignominy, meaning public shame or dishonour.

clue.text: Chaps engaged in major book of words, portentous?

indicators.note: engaged in means occupied within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the Oxford English Dictionary, the great book of words
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Men busy working on a big dictionary: an ominous sign?
explanation.definitionFit: Omened means bearing an omen, so it means foreboding or ominous, like portentous.

clue.text: Aids this barge being refitted — lakeside possibly

indicators.note: a boat being refitted has its parts reassembled in new places

parts.note: taken as written: the full set of letters
taken as written; these letters are taken out of the full set

explanation.surface: Help comes for this vessel being overhauled, perhaps at the edge of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: Aids plus this answer, rearranged, would spell lakeside, so remove the letters of Aids from it and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A keel is a flat-bottomed boat formerly used on the Tyne for carrying coal, a kind of barge.

clue.text: King set out for audience, one resisting conquerors from abroad

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: for an audience means as heard by listeners

parts.note: to have set out is to have left

explanation.surface: A monarch departs to address his people, a defender against foreign invaders.
explanation.definitionFit: A klepht was a Greek mountain brigand or guerrilla who held out against Ottoman Turkish rule.

clue.text: Whisky liquor that is taken after cocktail of bad rum

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters of bad rum rearranged
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A whisky drink is drunk after a cocktail of poor-quality rum.
explanation.definitionFit: Drambuie is a Scotch whisky liqueur sweetened with heather honey and herbs.

clue.text: Assistant brought up young parasitic worm

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means lifted, read from the bottom upward

parts.note: an aider is an assistant

explanation.surface: An assistant raised a young worm.
explanation.definitionFit: A redia is a larval stage of a fluke, a parasitic flatworm, developing inside a snail.

clue.text: Jock's stall — is this his den ransacked for merchandise?

indicators.note: a ransacked place is turned upside down, its contents jumbled

parts.note: taken as written; together with the answer forms the fodder
taken as written: the full set of letters

explanation.surface: A Scot's market booth has been raided by thieves after goods.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: the answer plus HIS DEN rearranged make MERCHANDISE. Jock is a crossword word for a Scot, signalling Scots dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Crame is a Scots word for a booth or stall where goods are sold.

clue.text: Can't stand to let off e.g. MOT?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to excuse from a test, like a vehicle's annual check

explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British vehicles; the question mark admits the invented sense of 'removing the test'.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to hate intensely, which is what someone who can't stand a thing feels.

clue.text: Sherry's medium in tradename large schooner

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: TN is the abbreviation for trade name

indicators.note: the medium of a word is its middle part

parts.note: the middle two letters of sherry

explanation.surface: A brand of sherry served in a big schooner glass.
explanation.walkthrough: A schooner is also a large sherry glass, which feeds the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A tern is a three-masted schooner, a kind of big sailing vessel.

clue.text: *A despicable person

parts.note: the asterisk marks the Azed competition word, for which solvers write their own clue
the setter supplies only a plain meaning: a contemptible wretch

explanation.walkthrough: In an Azed competition puzzle one clue is replaced by a bare definition; readers send in clues for it, and this is that entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Toerag is British slang for a worthless, contemptible scoundrel, so it names a despicable person.

clue.text: Former PM in charge of ideal state (before fall)

parts.note: Anthony Eden was British Prime Minister in the 1950s
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A past prime minister ran a perfect country, before his downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' suggests a politician's downfall; it is the Fall of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Edenic means like the Garden of Eden, the perfect paradise before humanity's expulsion.

clue.text: Noah's beginning to leave pens at being prepared for flood

indicators.note: something being prepared is worked into a new form
the beginning of a word, its opening letter, departs

parts.note: the first letter of Noah, removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Noah leaves his animal enclosures being made ready for the deluge.
explanation.walkthrough: Noah and pens look like the Ark story, which fits the flood.
explanation.definitionFit: A spate is a sudden flood of water in a river, from heavy rain.

clue.text: Ex-president (English not American) has installed Chinese interpreters

indicators.note: installed means placed within, so one piece is set inside
X not Y means the first letter stands where the second was

parts.note: Harry Truman, US president 1945 to 1953
E abbreviates English; replacing A for American
CH is the abbreviation for Chinese

explanation.surface: A former president, swapping an American for an Englishman, has hired Chinese interpreters.
explanation.walkthrough: The swap is one letter: the president's A for American becomes E for English before the Chinese abbreviation goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Truchman is an archaic word for a translator or dragoman, so truchmen are interpreters.

clue.text: Permit (one assumes) required before start of excavating Turkish borate

indicators.note: to assume something is to take it on, so one word holds another

parts.note: taken as written
one more is plus, and plus is and

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of excavating

explanation.surface: A mining permit is needed, so one supposes, before digging for a Turkish mineral.
explanation.walkthrough: The blog could not account for 'one' giving the inserted word, and this reading is a guess; the rest of the parse is secure.
explanation.definitionFit: Pandermite is a white calcium borate mineral named after Panderma, a port in Turkey where it is mined.
